title: Company-wide policies and process documentation
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended as the canonical reference for employees, people-ops, finance, and engineering teams.

Purpose:
- Provide a single, discoverable source of truth for cross-functional policies.
- Reduce ambiguity for approvers and owners by documenting thresholds, roles, and step-by-step procedures.
- Ensure consistent security posture and regulatory alignment across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Scope:
Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and third-party vendors who access company systems or represent Redwood in procurement, travel, or vendor engagements. Specific procedures for customer-sensitive private deployments are referenced in security-and-compliance pages.

Governance and ownership:
- People Ops: overall policy owner, travel & template maintenance.
- Finance & Legal: procurement, vendor contract approvals, expense reimbursements.
- Security: access control standards, privileged access reviews, data classification.
- Eng Platform & Eng Infra: change management for production systems and infra.

Quick reference table (owners & escalation):
- Access & Permissions — Owner: Security; Escalation: Director of Security
- Change Management — Owner: Eng Platform; Escalation: VP of Engineering
- Data Management — Owner: Security & Product; Escalation: Head of Applied ML
- Procurement & Expenses — Owner: Finance; Escalation: CFO
- Vendor Management — Owner: Legal & Finance; Escalation: General Counsel
- Travel Policies — Owner: People Ops; Escalation: Head of People Ops
- Internal Templates — Owner: People Ops; Escalation: People Ops Manager

1) Access & Permissions
Purpose: Ensure the right people have the right access for the right reason, using least privilege and auditability.
Key principles:
- Least privilege by default.
- Role-based access control (RBAC) for common roles; temporary elevated access via Just-In-Time (JIT) workflows.
- Quarterly access reviews for privileged groups.
- All access must be requestable through the company IAM portal and tied to an approved ticket.

Access request process (engineers & contractors):
1. Submit access request in IAM portal with rationale, duration, and approving manager.
2. Manager reviews and approves within 48 business hours; security must review for privileged requests.
3. IAM automates grant for standard roles; JIT for elevated roles issues time-limited credentials (max 8 hours).
4. Ticket must include required training completion where applicable (e.g., handling customer data).

Privileged access and emergency escalation:
- Privileged groups: infra-admins, production-ops, key-management-admins.
- Emergency access: request via on-call security channel and create retrospective ticket within 24 hours.
- Quarterly privileged access report owned by Security; anomalies investigated within 5 business days.

Access revocation
- Offboarding checklist (people-ops + manager): revoke SSO, remove from groups, reassign ownership, reclaim devices within 24 hours of termination.

2) Change Management
Purpose: Apply consistent controls for infrastructure and application changes to maintain availability and security while enabling rapid iteration.
Scope: All changes that touch production services, customer-facing APIs, networking, or IAM configuration.

Change categorization:
- Standard Changes: low-risk, pre-authorized (e.g., routine config updates below thresholds).
- Normal Changes: require CAB review if outside standard criteria.
- Emergency Changes: expedited path for incidents; retrospective review mandatory.

Change process (normal change):
1. Author creates a change RFC in the Change Registry (template attached in Templates section).
2. Pre-approval by service owner and SRE on-call.
3. Submit to weekly Change Advisory Board (CAB) or request fast-track review.
4. Approved changes scheduled in maintenance windows; runbook and rollback steps required.
5. Post-change validation and one-week monitoring window; close RFC after verification.

SLOs and thresholds:
- Changes that modify network ACLs, IAM policies, or kernel-level runtime require 48 hours lead time and SRE sign-off.
- Latency-affecting changes require a canary deployment (min 5% traffic) for 2 hours prior to full rollout.

Emergency change process:
- Triage by on-call, implement fix with minimal blast radius, document in RFC within 24 hours, schedule postmortem if incident triggered.

3) Data Management
Purpose: Protect customer and internal data through classification, handling rules, and retention policies.
Data classification levels:
- PUBLIC: safe to publish externally.
- INTERNAL: company-internal operational information.
- CONFIDENTIAL: customer or sensitive business data.
- RESTRICTED: regulated data or PII subject to legal/regulatory controls.

Handling rules (summary):
- CONFIDENTIAL & RESTRICTED data must be stored in approved encrypted buckets with IAM restrictions and audit logging enabled.
- Access approvals for CONFIDENTIAL/RESTRICTED require manager + security sign-off and data handling attestation.
- Data minimization: collect only required fields; purge test datasets that contain customer data after validation.

Retention & deletion:
- Default retention: INTERNAL 3 years; CONFIDENTIAL 7 years; RESTRICTED per contract/legal requirements.
- Data deletion requests: submit a ticket to Data Requests queue; Security coordinates verification and deletion within SLA (30 days for customer data requests).

Export & transfer controls:
- Cross-border transfers of RESTRICTED data require legal approval and documented transfer mechanism (SCCs, Standard Contractual Clauses).

Data incidents:
- Follow security incident response; notify Legal and Customer Success for customer-impacting events within 24 hours.

4) Procurement & Expenses
Purpose: Standardize purchasing approvals, expense reimbursements, and budget ownership.
Procurement thresholds & approvers:
- <$1,000: Requestor’s manager approval.
- $1,000–$25,000: Manager + Budget owner approval.
- >$25,000: Finance director + Legal (if contract).
- >$250,000: CFO and Executive approval.

Purchase process:
1. Create procurement request in Procurement Portal with business justification and GL code.
2. Finance validates budget and issues PO for approved purchases.
3. Vendor onboarding required if third-party (see Vendor Management).

Expense policy (employee reimbursements):
- Reimbursable items: travel (air, hotel), client meals (reasonable), equipment pre-approved by manager.
- Per diem: $75 domestic, $150 international (exceptions require People Ops approval).
- Submissions: submit receipt-backed expenses within 30 days; Finance processes reimbursements on biweekly payroll schedule.
- Non-compliant expenses may be declined and returned to the submitter.

5) Vendor Management
Purpose: Reduce supplier risk and ensure contractual protections (IP, security, SLAs).
Onboarding checklist:
1. Procurement request submitted and approved.
2. Security assessment (questionnaire + evidence) for vendors handling CONFIDENTIAL/RESTRICTED data.
3. Legal reviews and signs contract; include data processing agreement (DPA) when applicable.
4. Finance sets up vendor in AP system and issues PO.
5. Kickoff with vendor, assign internal vendor owner.

Ongoing vendor reviews:
- Annual risk re-evaluation for vendors with access to CONFIDENTIAL/RESTRICTED data.
- SLAs and performance metrics reviewed quarterly by vendor owner.
- Offboarding: revoke access, collect assets, close open POs within 30 days.

6) Travel Policy
Purpose: Safe, compliant, and cost-effective employee travel.
Booking & approvals:
- All travel requires manager approval and pre-trip registration in the Travel Portal.
- Lowest reasonable coach fares encouraged; upgrades require pre-approval and business justification.

Safety & incident response:
- People Ops maintains a travel watch and will contact travelers in region-level advisories.
- Emergency contact: People Ops travel coordinator.

Expense limits (examples):
- Hotel: up to $300/night domestic (higher in select metros with approval).
- Meals: per diem as above.

International travel:
- Passport & visa responsibility of traveler; business visa support coordinated by People Ops.
- Ensure appropriate data handling and device encryption while traveling.

7) Internal Templates and Attachments
Included templates (available in Templates library):
- Change RFC template (use for change requests)
- Procurement request form
- Vendor security questionnaire (questionnaire-vendor-2027.docx)
- Data access request template
- Travel pre-approval form

Template usage guidelines:
- Fill all required fields before submission; incomplete forms will be rejected by automated checks.
- Use standardized subject lines when emailing Finance/Legal to allow automated routing.

Appendices
A. Contacts & escalation matrix:
- People Ops: people-ops@example.redwood.ai
- Finance: procurement@example.redwood.ai
- Security: security-ops@example.redwood.ai
- Legal: legal@example.redwood.ai

B. Example change RFC checklist:
- Summary and motivation
- Impacted services and components
- Rollout plan and canary strategy
- Rollback plan and estimated blast radius
- Monitoring & post-deploy validation steps

C. Frequently asked questions (abridged):
Q: How long before a planned production change should I submit an RFC?
A: At least 5 business days for normal changes; 48 hours advance for network/IAM changes.

Q: Who signs off on vendor DPAs?
A: Legal is the signature authority; Finance initiates vendor setup after Legal approval.

Maintenance and review cadence:
- This document is reviewed annually by People Ops, Finance, and Security. Interim updates for regulatory or org changes will be published as needed.
